_meta.title: Shipped baseline seed — illustrative, not released
_meta.purpose: Enough for the product to run and be demonstrated before an operator has released anything. Every value here resolves with provisional: true and is labelled on every screen and in every response that reads it.
_meta.rule: A released baseline replaces this entirely for that metric and scope. The two are never merged.
_meta.register: Every entry here is a candidate the Baseline Register (docs/BASELINE-REGISTER.md, data/baselines/baseline-register.json) proposes for release, with its verification level in the source text. A secondary_reported entry is a figure quoted from a description of its source, not read from it — a demonstration runs on it; a disclosure does not, until an operator has re-read the figure and released it. A metric nothing reads yet is not seeded: its adopted candidate stays in the register until the engine that reads it exists.

baselines.source: CarbonIQ FinTech — this product's own carbon-intensity screen, not a taxonomy threshold. The Sri Lanka Green Finance Taxonomy (May 2022) sets no absolute kgCO2e/m² figure: its construction criteria are relative (M6.1 ≥30% PED reduction, M6.3 ≥10% below a nearly zero-energy benchmark) or certification-based (M6.2 Green SL Gold/Platinum).
baselines.note: Two band sets were live in this codebase and disagreed — 520/780 and 600/900 — so a building at 560 kgCO2e/m² was Green from one endpoint and Transition from another. 520/780 is now the single answer, held here so it can be released, versioned and superseded rather than edited in a constants file.

baselines.source: CarbonIQ FinTech — plausibility bands for a borrower's reported scope 1 and 2 intensity per million LKR of revenue, set at a quarter to four times the order-of-magnitude sector figure in data/pcaf-parta/sector-factors.json. PCAF sets no such test; the bands are regional judgement and are held here so they can be released, versioned and superseded with a reason.
baselines.note: A borrower outside its band is recorded as a finding and nothing is refused and no figure changes: the check exists to catch a unit or a boundary error, not to police a borrower.

baselines.source: Ember, Yearly Electricity Data, file of 23 Jun 2026 — Sri Lanka 2024 CO2 intensity 375.73 gCO2/kWh: generation-weighted average of all generation, CO2 only, no transmission-loss uplift; series 2019 518.30 · 2020 512.73 · 2021 418.05 · 2022 410.15 · 2023 417.33 · 2024 375.73 · 2025 321.16. Verification: primary (file read). https://storage.googleapis.com/emb-prod-bkt-publicdata/public-downloads/yearly_full_release_long_format.csv. Location-based; a borrower's scope 2 only, never a displacement factor. Replaced by a CEB/SLSEA-published average on release; update yearly.

IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Vol. 2 Energy, Table 1.4 default CO2 emission factors (kg/TJ: diesel 74,100 · petrol 69,300 · kerosene 71,900 · residual fuel oil 77,400 · LPG 63,100 · natural gas 56,100 · other bituminous coal 94,600) ÷ 277,777.8 kWh/TJ; CO2 only, net calorific value, 100 % oxidation. Verification: secondary_reported (table values to be re-read at https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2006gl/pdf/2_Volume2/V2_1_Ch1_Introduction.pdf). Sri Lanka has no biofuel blending mandate, so no biogenic deduction applies; a per-litre figure needs a Sri Lankan density from the SLSEA Energy Balance appendix.
baselines.authority: IPCC (the standard's value wins; the registry holds the citation)

baselines.source: Office: ~250 kWh/m²/yr (building energy index range 235–285) for air-conditioned multi-storey offices in Colombo, an 87-building study (~73,000 m²) cited by IESL SLEN 'Building Energy Standards/Codes: Present Status and Way Forward' and/or the University of Moratuwa thesis 'Electrical energy saving potential in Sri Lanka office buildings' — attribution to be confirmed by opening https://iesl.lk/SLEN/46/Energy.php and http://dl.lib.uom.lk/handle/123/12434. Supermarket: 465.4 kWh/m²/yr per total floor area (780.0 per sales floor), IEEE/University of Moratuwa 'Benchmarking Energy and Water Consumption of Supermarkets in Sri Lanka', n = 101, 2022, https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9906145/. Verification: secondary_reported. Types not held here (retail, hotel, industrial, residential) fall back to the provisional energy-statistics table and say so.

Annual distance per vehicle by class, Sri Lanka — World Bank / ESMAP 'Sustainable Transport Options for Sri Lanka' (ESM262), 2000 fleet: petrol car 8,274 km, diesel car 16,759, petrol three-wheeler 19,676, 4-stroke motorcycle 5,171 (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/503521468105868544/txt/ESM2620v10CE0S1e0Transport01public1.txt). Bus 61,509 km per SLTB fleet bus derived from NTC 2019 operated km over the average fleet, via mirror. Verification: secondary_reported; the only Sri Lankan per-class set found is a 2000 fleet and a disclosure resting on it says so. A Sri-Lanka-wide statistic is local under PCAF §5.6 fn 146, so make/model efficiency × this figure is Option 2a, score 2. Vans and lorries are not held (not verified) and fall back to the provisional vehicle-statistics table. docs/BASELINE-REGISTER.md §3.5.2.
baselines.authority: World Bank / ESMAP; National Transport Commission (derived)
